rubrics.justification: The response directly contradicts the provided lab grade 0DD by calling the embryo a good-quality early/full blastocyst with visible ICM and cohesive TE, which overstates morphology and likely fabricates favorable features.
It integrates age, ovarian reserve, semen, BMI, endometrium, and prior IVF outcomes well, though it builds some conclusions on an overly optimistic embryo assessment.

The reasoning is structured, but there is a major internal problem: it labels a 0DD embryo as good quality and then bases prognosis on that, creating a flawed logic chain and an arguably inflated implantation estimate.

It correctly notes Gardner grading concerns and appropriately discourages unsupported immune therapies, but it is not guideline-aligned to reinterpret a 0DD embryo as favorable morphology and to frame it as a good-quality transfer candidate.

The recommendations are practical and clinically usable, including SET, luteal support, and targeted future workup, though they are somewhat compromised by the inaccurate embryo-quality interpretation.
